stages.prompt: Two equal-length ribbons: one divided into 2 equal segments, the other into 4. Identify the whole before shading.
Predict whether shading 1/2 and 2/4 covers equal length. Save the prediction before manipulating.
Shade 1/2 and 2/4 on equal-length fraction bars; align endpoints; inspect partition changes.
Explain why 1/2=(2×1)/(2×2)=2/4; the whole stays fixed while the pieces change.
Investigate 2/3 versus 4/6 with the same fixed whole, recording a reason.
A peer claims 1/2 equals 2/3 by adding 1 to top and bottom. Test their claim.
Two identical routes have 3/6 and 4/8 marked. Explain whether marked lengths agree without a diagram.
Separate, novel backend-scored variant; no bar, hint, answer reveal or guided mastery credit.

diagnosis.observed: 1/2 equals 2/3 after adding one to each term
diagnosis.probe: On equal wholes, are the shaded lengths the same?
socratic: If one half is split into two pieces, how many pieces fill the whole?
How many equally sized pieces remain shaded?
diagnosis.repair: Repartition each half, keeping whole fixed.

diagnosis.probe: If a whole is divided into more equal slices, does each become larger?
socratic: Which segment is longer on an equal-length bar?
Where does one eighth land on a number line relative to one fourth?
diagnosis.repair: Compare equal reference wholes and their units.

diagnosis.observed: half a 12cm bar equals half a 20cm bar in physical length
diagnosis.probe: Did you hold the whole constant?
socratic: What is the whole in each diagram?
Would its length affect the shaded half?
diagnosis.repair: Normalize bar length before any equal-length claim.
diagnosis.unseen_recheck: Is half of 12cm physically equal to half of 20cm?

accessibility.screen_reader_equivalent: Narrate whole lengths, numerator/denominator and partition state
